recipes.title: Veggie Omelette
steps: Dice the pepper and roughly chop the spinach. Grate the cheddar.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and soften the pepper for 3 minutes. Add the spinach until just wilted, then tip onto a plate.
Melt the remaining butter, pour in the eggs and let them set at the edges for 1 minute, gently pulling the edges inward.
Scatter the vegetables and cheese over one half, fold over and slide onto plates.

recipes.title: Blueberry Overnight Oats
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds and honey together in a bowl.
Divide between two jars, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Top with blueberries just before eating, loosening with a splash of milk if too thick.

recipes.title: Avocado Toast with Fried Egg
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with the juice of half the lemon, salt and pepper.
Fry the eggs in the olive oil over medium heat until the whites are set but the yolks are runny.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with an egg and finish with chili flakes.

recipes.title: Chicken Caesar Wraps
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and pan-fry in the oil for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Shred the lettuce and shave the parmesan.
Toss the lettuce with the dressing.
Warm the tortillas, pile on lettuce, chicken and parmesan, then roll up tightly and halve.

recipes.title: Creamy Tomato Basil Soup
steps: Chop the onion and mince the garlic. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add most of the basil and blend until smooth with a stick blender.
Stir in the cream, season to taste and serve topped with the remaining basil.

recipes.title: Lemony Chickpea Feta Salad
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dice the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and thinly slice the onion.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toss everything together, crumble over the feta and serve.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Bolognese
steps: Finely chop the onion and carrot, and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and brown the beef over high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Remove excess fat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and 100 ml water, then simmer on low for 35–40 minutes, stirring now and then. Season well.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Garlic Salmon
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Halve the potatoes, toss with half the oil and salt, and roast on a sheet pan for 15 minutes.
Cut the broccoli into florets and mince the garlic. Mix the garlic with the remaining oil and the juice of half the lemon.
Add the broccoli to the pan and nestle in the salmon. Spoon the garlic mixture over everything.
Roast for 12–14 minutes until the salmon flakes easily.
Serve with lemon wedges from the remaining half.

recipes.title: Chicken & Veg Stir-Fry
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it according to the packet.
Slice the chicken into thin strips. Slice the peppers and carrot, cut the broccoli into small florets, and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Stir-fry the carrot and broccoli for 3 minutes, then the peppers, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the soy sauce and a splash of water and toss for 1 minute. Serve over the rice.

recipes.title: Smoky Three-Bean Chili
steps: Dice the onion and peppers, and mince the garlic.
Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the peppers and garlic and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, the drained and rinsed beans and chickpeas, and 150 ml water.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until thick, stirring occasionally. Season and serve.

recipes.title: Margherita Flatbread Pizza
steps: Heat the oven to its highest setting with a baking tray inside.
Divide the dough in two and stretch each piece thin on floured baking paper.
Crush the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and spread over the dough. Tear the mozzarella on top.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake for 8–10 minutes until the crust is blistered.
Finish with basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.title: Fluffy Banana Pancakes
steps: Mash one banana well and whisk with the milk and eggs.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt until just combined; lumps are fine. Rest for 5 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a pan over medium heat and cook ¼-cup scoops for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Slice the second banana and serve the stacks with the banana and maple syrup.

answer:
Your Recipes note is now a recipe and meal planning app. I only checked the recipe list on screen. The plan, shopping, cooking and edit screens compile but I haven't seen them rendered or clicked through.

- **Recipes:** twelve seeded recipes (omelette, overnight oats, avocado toast, Caesar wraps, tomato soup, chickpea salad, bolognese, salmon, stir-fry, chili, pizza, pancakes). You can search by title, tag or ingredient and filter by tag. A recipe opens with its ingredients and steps, and a serving stepper rescales the amounts. You can add, edit and delete recipes.
- **Cooking mode:** "Start cooking" shows one step at a time in large text with Back and Next buttons. You can switch to a scaled ingredient list, and it asks the device to keep the screen on.
- **Meal plan:** a week view with breakfast, lunch and dinner for each day. Tap the add button to pick a recipe, adjust servings per meal, and page between weeks. This week's plan (Mon 5 – Sun 11 Oct) is seeded.
- **Shopping:** ingredients from the week's plan are added up across recipes, scaled to the planned servings, and grouped by aisle. Items can be ticked off, and you can add your own (two are seeded: coffee beans and dish soap).

The app's accent colour comes from the note's theme. The preview flagged "New" and "All" as slightly below the recommended text contrast, and I left that alone.
